summary: Researched on the morning of Mon 23 Nov; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the final check. A thin Monday: Serie A, La Liga and Premier League evening games, AFC Champions League Elite, Allsvenskan, the Bulgarian league, Süper Lig, Ligue 2, Dota 2 BLAST Slam group deciders and one KHL game; basketball is not researched (the owner's permanent rule). Medium: Al-Ittihad (1xbet and a model near 72%), Hammarby (title race, DraftKings agrees), Ludogorets (only the under 4.5 goals leg is in range), Monza v Fiorentina (Fiorentina or draw; thin market) and Team Liquid (elimination decider, Thunderpick agrees). Low: Al Hilal (no second price, nothing verified), Nantes (depleted squads, models well under the market), NaVi (conflicting match dates, stale second price), Xtreme Gaming and Aurora (60-70% favourites with nothing independent confirming them), Başakşehir (price down 4.8% with no news, thin market), Severstal (goalies unconfirmed, a $390 market, a long trip east) and Brentford (top scorer suspended, Everton in form). Excluded: Levante v Elche (Valencian derby). Views that contradicted a game's own main risk were dropped (Al-Ittihad over 2.5, Hammarby over 2.5, Ludogorets over 1.5). Weekly review: no group is weak enough for a rule change; favourites priced 60-70% are on watch (58% hit vs 65% expected over 19 games).

checks.team_news: Fiorentina (Vanoli presser, 21 Nov, TMW): almost complete squad; Ndour back in group after ankle issue, Njie knock on Sweden duty described as not serious (final check), Atta fit but minutes managed (expected bench), Oulai and Fagioli back; no suspensions reported. Monza (Juric presser): Maye, Folorunsho and Ngonge out; Pessina available after two weeks of training, Ziolkowski back. One lineup source mentioned Juric as suspended, others do not; not confirmed, so no weight given.
checks.lineups: Not out yet; predicted XIs. Firenzeviola: Monza 3-4-2-1 Tornqvist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Lucchesi; Toure, Akinsanmiro, Colombo, Mangas; Mota, Robinson; Varela. Fiorentina 4-2-3-1 De Gea; Jimenez, Ranieri, Dragusin, Joao Mario; Ndour, Oulai; Mastantuono, Goncalves, Njie (or Gnonto); Pellegrino. Aggregated Italian previews agree on the shape; open spots are Gnonto/Njie and Pessina starting for Monza. Dragusin's availability is mentioned inconsistently (national-team duty in the presser vs listed in the XI), to be confirmed.
checks.rotation: No sign of rotation: Monza match is described as the first of four must-win games for Fiorentina. Last Fiorentina games: 2-2 vs Juventus (8 Nov), then international break; Monza lost 0-1 vs Atalanta (8 Nov). Equal rest, no midweek game, short domestic trip.
checks.motivation: ESPN standings before the game (12 rounds): Fiorentina 15th on 9 pts from 11 games, Monza 18th on 7 pts from 11 games. Both are in a relegation fight and both need the points, so no hard exclusion (favourite has not secured anything). Fiorentina are closer to safety; Monza are at home with little to lose.
checks.form: ESPN results, Fiorentina last 6 (league): D 2-2 Juventus, W 4-2 at Sassuolo, D 2-2 Atalanta, L 1-2 at Inter, L 1-3 Como, L 1-2 at Genoa: 1W 2D 3L, 12 goals for / 12 against, leaky and high-scoring. Monza last 6: L 0-1 Atalanta, L 1-2 at Bologna, L 1-4 Napoli, L 2-3 at Torino, W 4-0 Cagliari, L 1-3 at Lazio: 1W 5L, 9 for / 13 against. No xG found.
checks.h2h: Search snippets: Monza have beaten Fiorentina in only 1 of 7 meetings (Serie A and Serie B, last seen January 2025). Both sides' recent games are open (high scoring), so a draw or one-goal game is the main shape; no recent meeting data for 2026-27.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (source https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/ita.1/scoreboard?dates=20261123): Monza 3.50, draw 3.65, Fiorentina 1.91; de-vigged 0.264 / 0.253 / 0.483 (total 2.5). Opening: home 3.25, draw 3.55, away 1.91: Fiorentina unchanged, Monza drifted out (3.25 to 3.50). Polymarket: Fiorentina 0.495 now vs 0.495 24h ago (0% move), consistent with DraftKings within 1.5 points. Polymarket event volume about 4.8k USD (thin; the Fiorentina win market about 2.0k, draw market about 2.5k), liquidity about 438 USD-equivalent shown, so thin market.
checks.models: ClubElo fetch timed out, no bookmaker-free rating obtained. Proxy only: league table (Fiorentina +0 vs Monza -8 goal difference points gap 2) and form point to a small Fiorentina edge, not a large one.
checks.venue_weather: U-Power Stadium (Brianteo), Monza, normal home venue; kick-off Monday 23 Nov, 20:45 local (19:45 UTC); referee Daniele Doveri. No weather or pitch problem found, but weather was not checked for the day itself.

games.reason: Fixture verified on the ESPN scoreboard (Serie A, Monday 23 Nov 19:45 UTC, U-Power Stadium). No hard exclusion: both coaches are established (Juric at Monza, Vanoli at Fiorentina), no derby, no rotation announced, and both sides are in the relegation fight so the favourite is not coasting. DraftKings (0.483) agrees with Polymarket (0.495), the price is flat over 24h, and team news is clean for Fiorentina. Confidence is medium rather than high because the market is thin, no bookmaker-free rating was obtained, both sides are leaky and open, and the favourite is only at 49%. p is shaded slightly below the market toward the draw and the home side.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow Monza win: Fiorentina have won only 1 of their last 6 and conceded 12 goals in them, Monza are at home in a must-not-lose game under Juric, and Fiorentina's left-wing, Atta's minutes and Dragusin's availability are not settled. Double chance is exposed only to a Monza win (about 27%).

games.reason: Hard rule: derby or fierce rivalry. The fixture is real: ESPN esp.1 scoreboard for 20261123 lists Elche at Levante, 2026-11-23 20:00Z, Estadi Ciutat de València, status Scheduled. Spanish press calls Levante vs Elche a Valencian Community derby (derbi regional/autonómico): Alicante Plaza headlined 'Elche CF gana el derbi al Levante UD' for the first 2025/26 meeting, and Resumen Levante-Elche called the Jan 2026 3-2 a 'derbi de locura', with Levante winning in the 95th minute. The same press shows how volatile these meetings are: Elche won 2-0 away in 2025/26 and Levante won 3-2 late. I found no sacking or new coach, no neutral venue and no pitch problem. I did not run Stage 2 checks (lineups, odds move, models) because the derby exclusion decides it.
games.main_risk: Regional derby: the favourite Levante (about 0.45 on Polymarket, DraftKings de-vigged 0.435) faces high variance and a motivated Elche, and the draw is the likeliest failure for the Levante or draw / draw no bet legs. DraftKings has drifted from 2.15 to 2.20 for Levante.

checks.team_news: Brentford: Igor Thiago suspended (red card at Brighton; three-match ban, also misses Man Utd on 28 Nov), Aaron Hickey (hamstring, several weeks) and Nathan Collins (knee) out per the club preview and Racing Post; Rico Henry, Kaye Furo, Milambo and Carvalho listed out/doubtful by Squawka (the club says Carvalho may return to the squad); Dasilva a doubt (Dave Sport). Everton: no injuries reported, Jack Grealish available again after a club suspension, Moyes expected to have a fully fit squad. Brentford lose their top scorer and a centre-back; Everton are intact. No press-conference quotes read.
checks.lineups: Expected only, not confirmed. Racing Post: Brentford 4-2-3-1 Kelleher; Kayode, Ajer, Van den Berg, Lewis-Potter; Sangare, Janelt; Outtara, Jensen, Schade; Wilson (Callum Wilson replaces Thiago). Everton, Racing Post: Pickford; Rohl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Brentford club site (Connor O'Neill) gives a similar Everton XI with Dewsbury-Hall and George behind Barry. Both Everton sources agree.
checks.rotation: Monday night game (the last fixture of gameweek 11), played after the international break, so there is no midweek congestion for either side. Everton won their last three in all competitions. No rotation signs. Brentford's next game is Man Utd away on 28 Nov.
checks.motivation: Mid-table game with nothing decisive at stake. Brentford are 10th (10 played, 14 points, GD +5); Everton are reported sixth, two places above Brentford (Dave Sport; the page is internally inconsistent on the exact spot). Neither side has secured an aim, so there is no hard-exclusion case.
checks.form: Brentford: one win in six before the break, lost 2-0 at Brighton with a red card (first league away defeat since 9 May). Everton: unbeaten in their first six league games, one point from nine in October, then won their last three in all competitions (3-1 v Coventry, Thierno Barry 10 goals this season, four in the last three games). xG not found.
checks.h2h: 2025/26: Brentford won 4-2 at Everton (Thiago hat-trick) and drew 2-2 at home on 11 April 2026 (Thiago scored twice). Both teams scored in the last three meetings and Brentford are unbeaten in their last four. Thiago scored in both and is now suspended. Draws are plausible given the 2-2 and the level of the sides.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: 2.30 / 3.50 / 3.05, de-vigged 41.5 / 27.3 / 31.3. The opening line was 1.87 / 3.65 / 3.80, so Brentford drifted about 19 percent in price; this is explained by the Thiago ban, Hickey and Collins being out and Everton's form, not unexplained. bet365 (via Racing Post): Brentford 23/20 (2.15), draw 12/5 (3.40), Everton 23/10 (3.30), de-vigged about 43.8 / 27.7 / 28.5. Polymarket: Brentford 0.415 and flat over 24h (0.415 to 0.415), draw 0.275, Everton 0.305; Polymarket event volume is about $35k and about $24.5k on the Brentford win market, so the market is moderately thin. Two independent prices agree with Polymarket within 3 points. Racing Post's best tip is Everton at 23/10. No Stake or Rainbet prices seen.
checks.models: Brentford were not rated by ClubElo (the fetch failed with a 503/timeout), so no bookmaker-free Elo was read. The only bookmaker-free reference is Opta's predicted table cited in the Brentford club preview, which places Everton eighth. This check is incomplete.
checks.venue_weather: Gtech Community Stadium, Brentford (home), Monday 20:00 UTC, Sky Sports, referee Craig Pawson. A normal venue. No weather or pitch report was found, and no problem was reported.

games.reason: The fixture is verified (Premier League, Mon 23 Nov 2026, 8pm GMT at the Gtech Community Stadium). Keith Andrews has been Brentford coach since June 2025 and signed a new deal in February 2026, and David Moyes is Everton's manager, so there is no coach change. It is not a derby, there is no rotation, and the favourite still has something to play for, so no hard exclusion applies. Brentford are only a slight favourite at about 41.5 percent. Independent prices (DraftKings, bet365) agree with Polymarket within 3 points, and the drift from the opening line has a news explanation. Brentford are weakened without their top scorer Thiago, Collins and Hickey, while Everton are fit and in form, so I trimmed the home win and double-chance probabilities slightly below the market. Medium rather than high because lineups are unconfirmed, no Elo rating was read and the market volume is modest. Set to low when merged: news hurts the favourite (top scorer Igor Thiago suspended, Collins and Hickey out) against a fit, in-form Everton, which the rules make low.
games.main_risk: Everton win or draw: Brentford without Thiago (three-match ban), Collins and Hickey, a weaker side that took one win in six before the break and lost 2-0 at Brighton, against an in-form Everton led by Barry. A draw is the single most likely failure, given the 2-2 in April and a 27 percent draw price. Everton +1.5 fails only on a Brentford win by two or more, and Over 1.5 fails on a 0-0 or a 1-0.

checks.team_news: No roster change or stand-in reported for either side in the sources read today. Liquid: m1CKe, Malr1ne, Wisper, Boxi, tOfu (Liquipedia, Dotesports). DO KONCA, the former BetBoom stack: Kiritych, Save-, MieRo, Kataomi, kiyotaka (games.gg, Dotesports). Coach listings differ by source (boolk or TORONTOTOKYO for DO KONCA; Dukalis/Puppey or Blitz for Liquid). A Liquid web page I found still lists Nisha/Ace, but it is older and the other sources list the roster above. A stand-in could not be ruled out completely.
checks.lineups: Five players per side as in team_news, taken from tournament listings and match previews. No stand-in is mentioned in the Hotspawn or Kemosabe recaps of the Nov 22 series. The official pre-match roster is not yet visible this morning.
checks.rotation: Liquid played Nov 20 (2-0 over DO KONCA) and Nov 22 (1-2 loss to PARIVISION). DO KONCA beat LEGION 2-1 on Nov 22 in a do-or-die loser match. Both sides have played a series on each of the last two or three days; the schedule is equally dense for both.
checks.motivation: Group C decider: the winner takes 2nd place and moves to Last Chance, the loser is eliminated (esport.vision, Hotspawn). Both sides are 1-1 and both need it, so no hard exclusion applies. Liquid just lost the group-winner series and could be flat, which is a soft risk.
checks.form: Liquid: beat DO KONCA 2-0 on Nov 20 (two roughly 30-minute stomps), then lost 1-2 to PARIVISION on Nov 22, winning game 2 after a 21k net worth deficit and losing game 3 in about 38 minutes. Kemosabe's recap says Liquid could not win fights in game 3. DO KONCA: beat LEGION 2-1 on Nov 22 after losing to Liquid 0-2; described as having struggled all season and looked poor at 1win Essence III. GG score shows DO KONCA with a 20% win rate and a 3-loss streak, which includes older data.
checks.h2h: Liquid won 2-0 on Nov 20 at this event. Hotspawn cites a 7-2 head-to-head record for Liquid against this DO KONCA core. The BO3 format means a 2-0 or 2-1 result can go either way. DO KONCA took a game off LEGION and could do the same here.
checks.odds: Polymarket series winner: Liquid 0.745 now, 0.69 24h ago (volume about $11.7k on the main market, so reasonably liquid). The favourite's price rose 8% relative over 24h; the price history shows the move happened in the first few hours and has been flat at 0.745 since. I found no news explaining the rise, but it is a move in the favourite's direction, not against it. Second price: Thunderpick 1.32/3.24 (esport.vision), de-vigged Liquid 71.1% / DO KONCA 28.9%; another listing shows Thunderpick 1.27/3.53, de-vigged about 73.5%. Gap to Polymarket is 1 to 3.4 points, within 5, so p is set to 0.72, close to the bookmaker line. Polymarket also prices Liquid -1.5 maps at 0.445 and Over 2.5 maps at 0.44, so a 2-1 series is a live outcome.
checks.models: GosuGamers Elo for DO KONCA is 968 (world rank 62, CIS rank 37, 20% win rate), a low rating. I found no Elo for Liquid on the same scale. Dota2ProTips gave a pre-tournament 55/45 split for this matchup, which is much closer than the market, so the rating sources do not fully agree. Hotspawn and Freetips pick Liquid.
checks.venue_weather: BLAST Slam IX is played fully online (per Russian press via search summary), so there is no travel or venue factor. Ping and connection issues are the usual online risks.

games.reason: Liquid are the clear favourite: they beat DO KONCA 2-0 on Nov 20, DO KONCA has a weak rating, and an independent bookmaker price (Thunderpick, de-vigged 71 to 73.5%) sits within 5 points of Polymarket (0.745). p is set to 0.72 to reflect the bookmaker gap. Confidence is medium and not high because this is a BO3 where one lost game makes it a coin-flip decider, Liquid just lost to PARIVISION, the lineups and any stand-ins are not officially confirmed today, and the research record shows favourites at 60-75% underperforming.
games.main_risk: Liquid drop a game and lose a 1-2 series. DO KONCA are in a do-or-die spot, took a game off LEGION yesterday, and Liquid showed fragile team fighting in the 1-2 loss to PARIVISION. An unannounced stand-in is a smaller risk. The 8% rise in the favourite's price in 24h has no news explaining it.

checks.team_news: No stand-in or roster change reported for either side in the sources I could read. The Hawk Live match page lists NAVI as pma, Niku, daze, gotthejuice, Riddys and OG as something wrong, TOPSON, OneJey, Natsumi, skem. The metaratings preview lists the same NAVI five and OG as Natsumi, Topson, SSS, OneJey, skem. Liquipedia returned 403, so I could not read the official roster page. A roster search also returned older, conflicting NAVI lineups that I could not date.
checks.lineups: Five names per side from Hawk Live and cybersport.metaratings.ru. They match for NAVI. OG lists 'something wrong' on Hawk Live and SSS on metaratings. Not confirmed by Liquipedia or BLAST.
checks.rotation: Group stage of BLAST Slam IX (online). tips.gg lists the match as 14:00 GMT on 23 Nov. Hawk Live and metaratings list a NAVI vs OG group match on 20 Nov 2026, and Hawk Live shows NaVi 2-1 OG in its head-to-head table. I could not tell whether that is a stale or duplicate listing or a real earlier series, so I cannot say whether today's game is a rematch or what it is worth. Schedule density for NAVI is unknown.
checks.motivation: Format per tips.gg and esports.gg: 16 teams, four groups of four, all BO3, group winners go to the seeding matches and runners-up to Last Chance. I could not find Group A standings, so what NAVI or OG still need today is unverified.
checks.form: metaratings (20 Nov preview): NAVI won 4 of their last 5 series (3:1 GamerLegion, 2:0 Yellow Submarine, 2:0 GamerLegion, 2:0 Nemiga, lost 1:2 to Team Nemesis at Slam VIII). OG lost 4 of their last 5 (0:2 GamerLegion, 2:1 LEGION, 0:2 Yellow Submarine, 0:2 Team Liquid, 0:2 GamerLegion). OG are in poor form.
checks.h2h: Hawk Live: NaVi 1-0 OG (Slam VI, 4 Feb 2026), OG 1-0 NaVi (Slam V, Nov 2025), plus an entry of NaVi 2-1 OG dated 20 Nov 2026 that I could not verify. metaratings says 5 meetings, OG 3 wins and NAVI 2, and that the teams have not met with these rosters.
checks.odds: Polymarket: NAVI 0.715 now, 0.685 24h ago, a rise of 4.4% for the favourite (not a fall, so no price-move penalty). Volume not checked. The only second price is Winline/Pari NAVI 1.28 moneyline (about 78% before margin, de-vig not possible as the OG price was not stated), quoted in the 20 Nov preview for the match listed on that date, so it may be stale. data.odds from DraftKings is not available for this game. A second price from today is missing.
checks.models: No Elo or rating source was reachable (Liquipedia 403). Only the form record above.
checks.venue_weather: BLAST Slam IX is played entirely online, with no LAN finals (esports.gg via search snippet). No weather factor. Online play adds some noise.

games.reason: NAVI are the better team on recent form and the market favours them, but several key facts are unverified: the match date conflicts across sources (20 Nov vs 23 Nov, with a possible earlier NaVi 2-1 result), Group A standings are unknown, no rating source was reachable, and the only independent price is a pre-20-Nov quote. My p stays below the market because of this uncertainty.
games.main_risk: NAVI lose a BO3 to a poor-form OG (a 71% favourite in a best-of-three still loses about 3 times in 10), with the added uncertainty about whether this series is a rematch of an earlier 20 Nov game and what it is worth to each side.

checks.team_news: No roster change or stand-in reported for either side. Esport.vision/Dotesports list Xtreme Gaming as Ame, Xm, zeal, XinQ, BoBoKa (Dotesports adds Maps as coach, a conflict with one list that makes BoBoKa a player; no change announced). Team Nemesis: JaCkky, Ken, Jabz, Jhocam, NARMAN (coach Arthur per Dotesports; Liquipedia/GosuGamers say Astini, so the coach is unconfirmed). No injury or illness news found for either team. Not confirmed from an official team post.
checks.lineups: Dota has no lineup release. Both teams have used the same five players in their series at this event (Nemesis 2-0 Spirit, 0-2 GamerLegion; XG 0-2 GamerLegion, 2-1 Spirit). Draft and picks are unknown until the series.
checks.rotation: Both played two series on days 1-2 (Fri/Sat 20-21 Nov) and have had a rest day since. XG's last series (2-1 vs Spirit) had a 96-minute Game 3 with FPS and reconnect issues, a possible fatigue point but a day off helps. Nemesis lost 0-2 to GamerLegion on day 2. Winner goes to a Last Chance match on Wednesday.
checks.motivation: Group B decider, both teams 1-1 (GamerLegion 2-0, Spirit out). Winner takes 2nd place and goes to Last Chance; loser finishes 3rd and leaves the event. Equal elimination stakes, so no hard exclusion.
checks.form: XG: 0-2 GamerLegion, then 2-1 over Spirit after two comebacks (one from about 40k net worth down); Dota2ProTips calls them inconsistent, strong at farming but weak from behind. Nemesis: 2-0 Spirit (52-32, 45-23 kills), then 0-2 GamerLegion; earlier 0-2 to 1win at BLAST Slam VIII (Oct) and 1-2 to GamerLegion at PGL Wallachia S9 (Sep). Hotspawn calls Nemesis a 'coin flip at the moment'. Last-10-series list for both not fully verified.
checks.h2h: XG lead 2-0: 2-0 at PGL Wallachia S9 (24 Sep 2026) and 2-1 at PGL Wallachia S7 (Liquipedia, EGamersWorld). Hotspawn's Owen H still picks Nemesis 2-1 on 'fearless Dota' while calling XG the more experienced side and better on paper.
checks.odds: Polymarket series winner 0.625 XG / 0.375 Nemesis, volume about 27.5k USD (liquid enough). 24h move: 0.60 (22 Nov 07:00 UTC) to 0.625 (since 22 Nov 13:00), a +4.2% rise for the favourite, flat for the last 18h, no news found to explain it; it moved with the favourite, not against. Second price: Thunderpick 1.51 XG / 2.46 Nemesis (via Esport.vision/search snippet), de-vigged about 61.9% / 38.1%, within 1 point of Polymarket. Game-1 market 0.58 XG, Game-2 0.59 XG, handicap XG -1.5 at 0.35. No DraftKings data in the built-in data for this game.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free Elo found (GosuGamers/Datdota/Liquipedia not retrievable; Liquipedia returned 403). Dota2ProTips shows XG at a 45% win rate and Nemesis at 43%, with rank numbers that conflict with the market view, so no usable independent rating. Only the market (Polymarket plus Thunderpick) and the 2-0 h2h support XG.
checks.venue_weather: Mostly reported as an online event on EU West servers (Strafe, Esports Central, The Loadout); BLAST.tv lists BLAST Studios Copenhagen for 20-29 Nov, probably a stale entry, not confirmed. Online play means ping and connection issues are a small variance factor (a reconnect problem already hit XG's last series). Weather is not relevant.

games.reason: Fixture verified (Group B decider, BO3, 23 Nov 14:00 UTC, BLAST Slam IX). No hard exclusion: same five players on both sides, both teams face elimination, no coach or venue issue found. XG are favoured by two independent prices (Polymarket 62.5%, Thunderpick de-vigged 61.9%) and lead the h2h 2-0, but Nemesis beat Spirit 2-0 and XG's form is unstable, so p is lowered a little below the market. Set to low when merged: favourites priced 60-70% have underperformed (58% vs 65% over 19 games), and here no independent rating and no full last-10 form could be verified.
games.main_risk: Xtreme Gaming's inconsistency from behind and a coin-flip series against a fearless SEA side that beat Spirit 2-0, with a short best-of-three adding variance. Research record says favourites at 60-70% have underperformed (58% vs 65%). XG also just played a 96-minute game, and no independent Elo or full last-10 form was verified.

checks.team_news: No stand-in or roster change reported for either side. esport.vision's preview mentions no stand-ins, and the hotspawn decider preview names none. Aurora's regular five are listed as skiter, Mikoto, Ws, Mira, kaori. LGD's are Wits, SumaiL, Davai, Thiolicor, Sneyking. I did not find an official team post or Liquipedia page confirming either five (Liquipedia returned 403).
checks.lineups: Rosters come from a single aggregated search summary of esport.vision and Liquipedia-style listings, not an independently confirmed pair of sources. No stand-in is flagged for this event. Not cross-checked, so only partly verified.
checks.rotation: BLAST Slam IX Group D decider on Day 4 (23 Nov 17:00 UTC). Aurora went 1-1 in the group (beat Astra Invicta 2-1, lost 0-2 to 1w Team). LGD also went 1-1 (lost 0-2 to 1w Team, beat Astra Invicta 2-1). Both have played two series this week, so schedule density is equal. The tournament runs 20-29 Nov, so this is not a long, fatiguing day for either team.
checks.motivation: Equal stakes: it is an elimination decider. The winner takes 2nd in Group D and goes to Last Chance on 24 Nov. The loser finishes 3rd and is out. Neither side has anything secured, so the hard no-stakes exclusion does not apply.
checks.form: Aurora are in a rough patch since patch 7.42. They barely beat Astra Invicta 2-1 and were swept 0-2 by 1w Team, and hotspawn says they have not adapted well. Hotspawn still ranks Aurora among the top five teams in the world and picks Aurora 2-1. LGD show the same group results (0-2 vs 1w Team, 2-1 vs Astra Invicta). Earlier this year LGD finished BLAST Slam VII group stage 8-3 and Aurora 6-5. Last-10-series detail was not obtained.
checks.h2h: Three recent meetings found, all BLAST Slam: 27 May Slam VII group stage LGD won 1-0 (BO1), 6 Jun Slam VII lower-bracket semifinal LGD won 2-1 (Aurora took game 1, LGD won the decider), 9 Oct Slam VIII playoffs Aurora won 2-0. That is 2 series to 1 for LGD, so LGD have beaten Aurora before and the pairing is close.
checks.odds: Polymarket series winner Aurora 0.595 / LGD 0.405 (event 1444824). 24h move is mild: 0.585 to 0.595, up 1.7% relative, so no unexplained drop. Series market volume is only about $5.0k, a thin market (event total about $6.6k). The Game Handicap Aurora -1.5 trades at 0.315. Second price, Thunderpick via esport.vision: Aurora 1.65 / LGD 2.14, de-vigged about 0.564 / 0.436. One other quoted price of Aurora 1.59 / LGD 2.24 de-vigs to about 0.585 / 0.415, but that snippet does not name its bookmaker or confirm it is for this match. The independent Thunderpick price is about 3 points below Polymarket for Aurora, within the 5-point range. DraftKings/ESPN data is not available for Dota.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating found. No GosuGamers or Datdota Elo retrieved, and Liquipedia and egamersworld returned 403. Only qualitative hotspawn view: Aurora top-five team, a scrappy series that can go either way. The 3-point gap to the de-vigged bookmaker price is the only quantitative cross-check.
checks.venue_weather: BLAST Slam IX is an online tournament, so there is no travel or weather. Online play can add connection and ping variance.

games.reason: Fixture verified: Aurora vs LGD Gaming is the BLAST Slam IX Group D elimination decider, BO3, 23 Nov 17:00 UTC, online. No hard rule applies, since both sides are fighting for survival and there is no coaching or roster news. I lowered Aurora from 0.595 to 0.57 because Thunderpick de-vigs to about 0.564 and Aurora are out of form on patch 7.42. The favourite is not strong enough to rate medium: Aurora lost 0-2 to 1w Team, LGD beat them 2-1 in June, no rating model was found, rosters are not independently confirmed, and the Polymarket series market is thin at about $5k. The research record also shows 60-70% favourites underperforming.
